9:30 am local: The equation is simple as we enter Day 4 if the Rawalpindi Test. Sri Lanka's lead is 82 and they have just one second innings wicket left. Their only hope of extending this lead is Milan Rathnayake. The bowling all-rounder batter very positively yesterday and raised his 2nd Test half-century. How many more runs can he add today? Pakistan have a history of being poor chasers in the 4th innings, but the visitors will need nothing short of a miracle to win this Test. We will get to know in a couple of hours.

And there comes the moment! Babar Azam collects the series trophy before being joined by his teammates for the celebrations. Azan Awais and Mohammad Taha hold the trophy, while the players flash smiles, thumbs-up signs and victory gestures for the cameras.

Pakistan's pace attack deserves immense credit for this victory. Saqib Khan, Mohammad Abbas, Razaullah and Aamer Jamal all played their part, but the efforts of the latter three deserve special recognition. Saqib's hamstring injury after just 1.2 overs in the second innings left Pakistan a seamer short, yet Abbas, Razaullah and Jamal refused to let that setback affect their intensity. Having dismissed Sri Lanka in just 35.3 overs in the first innings, they had to dig much deeper the second time around, with the visitors batting for 95 overs. The three seamers bowled long, demanding spells and kept coming back for more, and their extraordinary perseverance ultimately proved decisive in securing this win.
